For DAWN AI STUDY, the fellowship will provide a 12-month intensive incubation phase followed by six months of post-incubation growth support."

title: Terra Industries — Seed Round Close, 2026
description:
Verbatim from the source:

> Terra Industries, a Nigerian defence-technology startup that builds autonomous security systems using its proprietary software, has raised an additional $18 million, closing Africa's largest seed round at $52 million.
>
> Norleo Space Investments and angel investor Grant Gordon participated in the round as new investors alongside existing investors 8VC, Silent Ventures, Nova Global, Belief Capital, and SV Angel.
>
> Terra said in a statement that it will use the capital to open its first international office in London, expand its manufacturing capacity, accelerate deployment of its products across the Global South, and grow its team in the engineering, operations, and business development departments.

title: CardinalStone Finance — Nomba cross-border payments debt facility, 2026
description: "Nomba, a Nigerian fintech that enables businesses to collect payments and access banking services, has raised a $3 million debt facility through CardinalStone Finance Company Limited, the financing arm of CardinalStone Group, to expand its cross-border payments infrastructure across Central Africa. The company said the debt facility will give it more USD liquidity to deploy through its banking relationships in Hong Kong and Singapore. With more liquidity available across currencies, the company can support more transactions and settle payments to deepen existing trade corridors and expand into new ones."

title: Village Capital — Africa Ecosystem Catalysts Facility, first Nigeria investments, 2026
description: "Village Capital, a global nonprofit that backs high-impact startups, has deployed $450,000 from its Africa Ecosystem Catalysts Facility into two Nigerian startups, marking the investment vehicle's entry into the country after backing two Ghanaian companies earlier this year. The backed companies include Trade Lenda, a digital financial services platform for small and medium-sized businesses, and AirSmat, a climate-tech company that turns agricultural waste into biochar-based fertiliser. The latest investments bring the facility's total portfolio to seven startups across Ghana and Nigeria. Village Capital launched the $4 million facility in July 2025 with backing from the Dutch Entrepreneurial Development Bank (FMO) and the Netherlands Enterprise Agency (RVO)."

title: AfricInvest FIVE leads growth round in BFREE pan-African credit management fintech
description: AfricInvest's Financial Inclusion Vehicle (FIVE) leads a growth round in BFREE, a Lagos-based pan-African technology-enabled platform focused on acquisition and servicing of non-performing unsecured retail and SME loan portfolios. BFREE uses proprietary data infrastructure and AI-powered credit risk management to help financial institutions manage distressed credit. Managing over 10 million borrower accounts across 35+ transactions at time of investment. Co-investors include Algebra Ventures (first Nigeria investment), Capria Ventures, VestedWorld, Axian CVC, Angaza Capital, 4Di Capital, and DotExe Ventures.

title: European Union — Nigeria digitalisation (Global Gateway), 2026
description: "The European Union (EU), on Monday, announced a new investment package of EUR 290 million to be immediately mobilised in seven new operations in digitalisation, health and agricultural value chains... in the framework of the EU Global Gateway strategy." "The package of investments includes an additional EUR 131 million in the digitalisation sector, which will support the upgrade of digital connectivity and enhance digital services and skills." "Together with the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development, the EU will contribute to the roll-out of 90,000 km of fiber optic cable across the country." "The EU will help develop secure and interoperable digital public infrastructure and data exchange systems for digital services to citizens and in the framework of Nigeria's 3 million Technical Talent programme."

title: African Development Bank — Nigeria Project BRIDGE (D-VIBE) fibre expansion, 2026
description:
"The African Development Bank (AfDB) has approved a US$200 million loan towards Nigeria's Digital Value Chain Infrastructure for Boosting Employment (D-VIBE) project, also known as Project Bridge, a fiber-optic program aimed at expanding broadband access as well as strengthening the country's digital economy."

"The loan will help Africa's most populous country deploy 90,000km of open-access fiber nationwide, expand digital skills and drive job creation... extending Nigeria's national fiber backbone from around 30,000km to about 120,000km, connecting all 774 local government areas."

"The bank said the loan is part of an $800 million sovereign financing package for the project, alongside $500 million from the World Bank and $100 million from the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD). It added that the total project financing is estimated at $2 billion, and includes an EU grant of €22 million, a $2.6 million Multilateral Cooperation Center for Development Finance (MCDF) project preparation grant, and at least $1.2 billion investment from the private sector."

title: Nigeria Sovereign Fibre Project (Project BRIDGE)
description: Provision of a sovereign loan of up to USD 100 million to the Federal Republic of Nigeria to finance its participation in a special purpose vehicle (SPV) for the nationwide rollout of approximately 90,000 km of fibre-optic broadband infrastructure. The project supports Nigeria's National Broadband Plan, targeting connectivity for 50% of 33 million unserved Nigerians and raising fixed broadband penetration. SPV will operate as open-access wholesale provider. Co-financed in parallel by World Bank (USD 500m) and AfDB (USD 200m). Supported by EUR 22m EU grant for technical designs and capacity building for 2,000 technicians.

title: Google.org -- Africa AI Upskilling Programme (AAUP), Nigeria launch
description: "Google.org has committed $1.1 million to FATE Foundation to launch an advanced AI training program at 10 Nigerian universities in partnership with the African Institute for Mathematical Sciences. The initiative -- the Africa AI Upskilling Programme (AAUP), launched Monday at the University of Lagos -- is part of a broader push to build AI capacity across Africa... It starts in Nigeria but will ultimately cover 30 higher institutions across Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya and South Africa" (10 in Nigeria, 10 in South Africa, 6 in Kenya, 4 in Ghana), aiming to train more than 30,000 students.

title: Gates Foundation and MTN Group Foundation — Nigeria Maternal Health Multiplier, 2026
description: "MTN Group Foundation (MTN) and the Gates Foundation announced a strategic partnership to launch the Nigeria Maternal Health Multiplier, a first-of-its-kind initiative in Nigeria to improve maternal health outcomes through an integrated digital ecosystem that connects women, frontline health workers, and primary health care facilities." "It will expand equitable access to high-quality maternal health care through three components: AI-enabled, phone-based decision support tools for both frontline health workers and mothers, affordable smartphones and mobile data, and improved connectivity at health care facilities." "The four-year partnership was announced at Semafor's Next 3 Billion event, on the sidelines of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly in New York. It begins with an initial investment of approximately US$25 million between 2026 and 2030, including direct and in-kind contributions from the Gates Foundation and MTN. This anchor investment is intended to catalyze additional funding and support future expansion into other markets over time." Targets: "By 2030, the initiative aims to help 500,000 women access trusted health guidance, equip 5,000 frontline health workers with tools to identify complications from pregnancy and childbirth early, and enable 500 health facilities to deliver more consistent, higher-quality maternal health care."

title: U.S. Department of State — Nigeria health data systems under the America First Global Health Strategy MOU, 2025
description:
Section 2.5.3: "The U.S. Government intends to provide the following amount of funding for data systems in each of the specified years, subject to the availability of funds: 2026 $60,000,000; 2027 $49,000,000; 2028 $42,000,000; 2029 $23,000,000; 2030 $22,000,000", against Nigerian co-funding of $13,793,103 (2026) rising to $33,817,048 (2030). In 2026 the US line includes "$1.35M for NigeriaMRS, $1.05M for LAMISPlus, $0.38M for ViVA EMR".

The target is the Nigeria Digital Health Architecture's three exchanges - health information, health services and health insurance claims - into which government EHRs, TB and HIV systems, the National Data Repository, the LMIS, state EHRs and SORMAS are expected to integrate (2.5.1). The US also supports National Health Insurance Authority partnership with US firms "(i.e. AWS)" for data warehousing and cloud storage of the NHIA claims database.

The sum is one line of a wider MOU whose total planned US support is US$1,953,530,560 against Nigeria's US$2,975,634,499 (Appendix 1). Non-binding: "This MOU is not an international agreement" (6.9). The text is stamped NOT FOR PUBLIC RELEASE on every page.

title: LeapFrog investment in Moniepoint Group Nigeria Series C extension 2025
description: LeapFrog Investments participates in the USD 90 million extension of Moniepoint Group's Series C funding round in October 2025, co-investing alongside DPI (round lead), Visa, IFC, Google's Africa Investment Fund, Proparco, Swedfund, and others. Moniepoint is Nigeria's leading business banking, payments and credit unicorn, processing 5.2 billion transactions in 2023. Total Series C reaches USD 200 million (USD 110M in 2024 plus USD 90M in 2025). LeapFrog's specific share within the extension is undisclosed.

title: OmniRetail Digital B2B Commerce and Embedded Finance — Nigeria/West Africa
description: Norfund USD 7.5 million equity (co-led with Timon Capital) in USD 20 million Series A for OmniRetail. Nigerian digital B2B commerce platform providing informal retail shops with BNPL credit, digital payments, and fast delivery. OmniPay processed NGN 1.3 trillion (~USD 810M) transactions in 2024. Norfund's first direct equity investment in African fintech. Digital scope: B2B e-commerce, embedded finance (BNPL), POS payments, digital merchant credit scoring.

title: Moniepoint Digital Payments Equity Investment
description: Swedfund invested USD 10 million in equity in Moniepoint, described as Africa's fastest growing fintech company, to accelerate access to banking and digital payment solutions for Nigeria's underbanked MSMEs. Moniepoint has over four million business users and provides tailored financial products and services delivered via an extensive local distribution network. The investment is alongside DPI, IFC and Proparco.

title: Visa Strategic Investment in Moniepoint Nigeria
description: Visa made a strategic equity investment in Moniepoint Inc., Nigeria's fastest-growing fintech unicorn (valued >$1 billion), as part of Moniepoint's Series C funding round in January 2025. The investment exceeded $10 million. Moniepoint serves 2.5+ million business owners in Africa with payment solutions, business banking, and financial tools. Visa's investment is intended to accelerate financial inclusion for African SMEs and expand Moniepoint's operations across Africa.

title: Airtel Nigeria — Eko Atlantic 38MW hyperscale data centre, 2025
description:
"Airtel Nigeria plans to build a carrier-neutral 38MW hyperscale data centre in Eko Atlantic City in Lagos to meet surging demand for cloud and AI services. Part of Airtel's broader Nxtra network, the facility will handle next-generation compute workloads including GPU-powered infrastructure for AI. It will host over 3,000 racks across six floors..."

"Airtel Nigeria CEO Dinesh Balsingh told a media briefing in Lagos that the data centre will cost over US$120 million and was scheduled for completion in Q1 2026."

title: Equinix LG3 Lagos New Data Centre — $22 Million Investment
description: Equinix announced in November 2025 plans to build LG3, its first newly-constructed data centre in West Africa, at a cost of US$22 million. Set to open in Q1 2026, LG3 is the first phase of a US$100 million investment plan to transform Africa's digital landscape over the next two years. LG3 is located in Lagos, Nigeria and will deliver new colocation capacity supporting Nigeria's strategic position as an international hub for subsea cable connections. The $100 million plan includes expansions at existing sites in Nigeria, Ghana, and Côte d'Ivoire, as well as a new facility in Port Harcourt (PR1) serving as a 2Africa cable landing station.

title: EAIF — WIOCC senior secured loan for Nigerian fibre-to-the-home, 2025
description:
Verbatim from the financier's own release:

> London, December 15: The Emerging Africa & Asia Infrastructure Fund (EAAIF), a Private Infrastructure Development Group (PIDG) company, managed by Ninety One, today announced a $15 million investment in West Indian Ocean Cable Company (WIOCC), a key pan-African telecommunications infrastructure provider.

> EAAIF’s portion of the funding will support the rollout of fibre to the home networks in Nigeria, addressing the country’s rapidly growing demand for reliable, high-speed internet.

> All financing arrangements, including EAAIF’s $15 million senior secured loan facility, have a 10-year tenor and are structured as sustainability-linked facilities.

title: European Union — Nigeria Digital Economy Package (connectivity, DPI, skills), 2025
description: "Nigeria has secured a major boost for its digital transformation agenda as the European Commission announced a €45 million commitment under the EU–Nigeria Digital Economy Package. The announcement was made on Tuesday in Brussels during the EU–Nigeria Digital Open Day". Discussions focused on three areas: "Secure Connectivity and Digital Infrastructure" (nationwide fibre backbone, subsea cable capacity, 5G, last-mile access); "e-Governance and Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI)" (digital identity systems, interoperability frameworks, e-payment infrastructure); and "Digital Skills and Talent Development" (the 3MTT programme).

recipient: Federal Government of Nigeria / BRIDGE Project company
title: World Bank (IDA) — Nigeria BRIDGE nationwide broadband fibre project, 2025
description: "Nigeria has begun the financial advisory process for its ambitious plan to deploy 90,000 kilometres of fibre-optic cable under the $2 billion Building Resilient Digital Infrastructure for Growth (BRIDGE) Project, supported by the World Bank." "As part of the agreement with the Bank, which has already approved $500 million in financing, the government is required to appoint a financial advisory firm." "The BRIDGE Project, approved by the World Bank Group Board of Directors on October 8, 2025... Funding will be disbursed in five tranches, with the first $150 million going toward the company's initial equity capitalisation." The financing agreement with IDA was signed 30 December 2025; the Federal Government holds a 49% stake channelled through the Ministry of Finance Incorporated (MOFI). The programme deploys about 90,000 km of fibre "built around seven national rings, 37 metropolitan loops, 77 regional networks, and multiple edge data centers" (We Are Tech Africa), narrowing the broadband gap in underserved regions.

Norrsken22 is a returning investor from Sabi's earlier $20M 2022 venture round. Co-investors include CommerzVentures, Fluent Ventures, Proof VC, CRE Venture Capital and Janngo Capital.

title: Moove Mobility Fintech Equity Investment (Mubadala-led round)
description: Mubadala Investment Company led an equity and debt financing round for Moove, a Nigeria-founded mobility fintech providing vehicle financing to drivers of ride-hailing platforms including Uber. The total package was USD 76M comprising USD 28M in equity (new and existing investors led by Mubadala), USD 10M in venture debt managed by BlackRock, and USD 38M in previously undisclosed prior-period funds. Mubadala's specific own equity contribution within the USD 28M tranche is not separately disclosed; estimated at ~USD 14M (50% of tranche as lead investor). This was Mubadala's first investment in an African-founded startup. Moove operates in Nigeria, South Africa, Ghana and other markets. Mubadala later participated in Moove's Series B (March 2024, USD 100M led by Uber), which is not separately recorded as Mubadala's incremental commitment in the follow-on is also undisclosed.

The fund addresses structural challenges in healthcare, commerce, and finance through technology. Ventures Platform portfolio includes notable Nigerian tech companies such as Paystack, Mono, 500 Chow, and others.

description: The Action aims to support the improvement of Nigeria’s digital innovation ecosystem. It is part of the EU Action Document on supporting Innovation and Jobs for Youth in Nigeria (INN-JOBS). The Action will strengthen the EU's

title: AfricaGrow LP commitment to Ventures Platform Pan-African Fund I
description: AfricaGrow commits to Ventures Platform's $46M Pan-African Fund I, a leading early-stage VC firm focused on Nigeria and broader Africa. Fund invests in fintech, insurtech, health tech, edtech, agritech, enterprise SaaS. AfricaGrow confirmed LP alongside IFC, BII, Proparco, Standard Bank. Fund closed Dec 2022 above $40M target.

title: LeapFrog and Tana Africa Capital $110M joint investment in Interswitch digital payments Nigeria
description: LeapFrog Investments and Tana Africa Capital make a joint strategic investment of USD 110 million in Interswitch Group, one of Africa's leading technology-driven integrated digital payments companies. The investment involves both primary capital and acquisition of shares from existing shareholders including Ignite Holdco (Helios Investment Partners and TA Associates). Interswitch provides payment processing, switching services, card issuance and digital financial services across Nigeria and Sub-Saharan Africa, supporting financial inclusion for Nigeria's unbanked consumers.

title: Nigeria Digital Identification for Development (ID4D)
description: Sovereign loan to support harmonisation of Nigeria's digital identification system, enabling all persons in Nigeria to obtain a single unique official identifier for access to public and private services. Co-financed with the World Bank (P167183).

recipient: Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC) / MTN Nigeria Communications PLC
title: MTN Nigeria 5G Spectrum Licence — 3.5GHz NCC Auction
description: MTN Nigeria Communications PLC acquired a 100 MHz TDD 5G spectrum licence (Lot 1, 3500-3600 MHz) from the Nigerian Communications Commission following the December 2021 auction. The winning bid was $273.6 million; MTN also paid an additional $15.9 million at the assignment stage to secure its preferred Lot 1 band position, bringing total payments to $289.5 million. Full payment was confirmed by NCC on 24 February 2022. MTN became Nigeria's first operator to launch commercial 5G services (August 2022). The licence enables 5G network rollout across Nigeria, supporting mobile broadband, IoT, and enterprise digital services.

recipient: TIDE Africa II LP (TLCom Capital Nigeria)
title: TLCom TIDE Africa II — LP Commitment (Africa Tech VC Fund)
description: BII committed $10M to TLCom TIDE Africa II LP in November 2021. TLCom is an Africa-focused venture capital investor that supports early-stage tech businesses. TIDE Africa II continues TLCom's mandate to invest in tech-enabled businesses across SSA, with a focus on Nigeria and other high-growth African tech ecosystems. The fund targets fintech, logistics, health-tech, and digital platforms.

description: IFC committed $10 million as a limited partner in TIDE Africa II Limited Partnership, an Africa-focused venture capital fund investing in Seed to Series A tech and tech-enabled companies mainly in East and West Africa. TIDE II is managed by TLCom Capital, one of Africa's most prominent early-stage technology venture investors. The fund targets fintech, logistics tech, health-tech, edtech, and digital platforms. Co-investors include BII, FMO, Proparco, and DEG. This is IFC's second investment in TLCom funds (following the $15M commitment to TIDE Africa I managed by BII).

title: Nigeria National Social Safety Net Program-Scale Up — Digital Delivery Component
description: Component 3 of the $800M National Social Safety Net Program Scale-Up finances digital delivery systems for cash transfers: digital payment infrastructure, biometric-linked beneficiary accounts, electronic payment mechanisms. All transfers are digitally delivered to beneficiary-owned accounts backed by biometric ID. $53M of $800M total.

title: AfricInvest investment in PalmPay Nigeria digital payments platform Series A $100M
description: AfricInvest participates in PalmPay's USD 100 million Series A funding round (closed August 2021) alongside Chuangshi Capital, Yunshi Equity Investment Management, Trust Capital and Chengyu Capital. PalmPay is a Nigerian digital payments and financial services platform offering zero-fee transfers, bill payments, mobile money, merchant POS acquiring, digital wallets, and lending services. Company operates via the Cathay AfricInvest Innovation Fund (CAIF). PalmPay subsequently became one of Africa's fastest-growing fintechs with over 35 million registered users.

title: Moniepoint — Equity Investments (B2B Payments & Digital Banking Platform)
description: Three equity investments by BII in Moniepoint (formerly TeamApt), a Nigerian fintech providing an all-in-one payments, banking, and operations platform for businesses. Moniepoint processes millions of transactions monthly for small businesses across Nigeria. Investment 1: $3.6M (Sep 2021, via VC Scale-up programme). Investment 2: $1.5M equity (Jan 2022, follow-on). Investment 3: $5M equity (Jun 2022, Moniepoint Inc. later exited Oct 2024). BII investment improved access to financial services for millions of unbanked individuals and micro-entrepreneurs.

title: Novastar leads Moniepoint Series B — Nigerian digital financial services platform
description: Novastar Ventures leads a $30M Series B round for TeamApt (now Moniepoint), Nigeria's leading business banking and agency banking platform providing financial services to the mass market. Moniepoint serves 600,000+ businesses and millions of unbanked customers via agency banking, mobile banking, POS and payment processing. Round also includes FMO, Global Ventures, British International Investment, Oui Capital, Kepple Africa Ventures and Endeavor Catalyst. Moniepoint later achieved unicorn status ($1B valuation) in its 2024 Series C.

title: NIGERIA TELECOM EXPANSION
description: Capacity and coverage expansion of the promoter's 4G mobile broadband access network to address high growth in mobile data applications. EIB financing to upgrade the 4G core mobile broadband network and expand radio network coverage from 90% to 98% of population in Lagos region. Mobile broadband services to reach remaining areas without access.

title: Project for Building Foundations Towards Digital Governance in Nigeria (Phase 2)
description: KOICA grant to Nigeria ($13M, 2020-2026) to enhance capacity for e-government master plan execution, improve e-government service delivery competencies, activate the Government Service Portal (www.services.gov.ng), and establish additional NIN enrolment centres. Phase 1 (2013-2019) established the e-Government Training Centre.

description: TLcom Capital participated as an existing investor in uLesson's $7.5M Series A round, approximately 11 months after leading the seed. uLesson had grown to cover K-12 content across six African countries. title: Nigeria Digital Identification for Development Project
description: Provides digital identification for over 150 million Nigerians to expand financial inclusion and improve access to public services. Supports national ID enrollment, harmonization of existing ID systems, and development of digital authentication infrastructure.

title: NIGERIA DIGITAL ID
description: Framework Loan for development of a digital identity (eID) infrastructure in Nigeria and supply of biometric identity to people residing in Nigeria and Nigerians living abroad. Project provides platform for economic development. Identification central to delivering government services: education, health, social safety, transportation, finance, elections. Supports Nigeria's digital economy and fiscal management. Co-financed with World Bank IDA and AFD.

title: Actis acquisition of controlling stake in Rack Centre Nigeria (pan-African data centre platform)
description: Actis takes a controlling stake in Rack Centre, Nigeria's leading carrier-neutral co-location data centre in Lagos, as the anchor investment of a US$250 million pan-African data centre platform established jointly with Convergence Partners. Rack Centre hosts over 80 international, regional and local clients including carriers, cloud providers and hyperscalers. Platform strategy: buy-and-build, targeting carrier-neutral data centres across key African markets. Actis partnered with Convergence Partners as ICT infrastructure expert and Tim Parsonson (Teraco co-founder) as chairman.

recipient: Unnamed Nigerian telecoms company (borrower not publicly disclosed)
title: Nigeria Telecoms Equipment Senior Debt Facility (Syndicated)
description: AFC provided and successfully syndicated funded participations under a USD 95 million senior debt facility to finance the supply of equipment to a leading telecoms company in Nigeria. This is disclosed on AFC's syndications page as a completed transaction, with AFC acting as arranger. The borrower's identity is not publicly disclosed but is described as a 'leading telecoms company in Nigeria'. The facility is distinct from the MTN Nigeria equipment deal and supports mobile network infrastructure deployment.

title: DCCP Nigeria - Digital Connectivity and Cybersecurity Partnership
description: USAID Digital Frontiers DCCP activity in Nigeria supporting digital connectivity policy, broadband regulatory reform, and cybersecurity capacity building.

title: Bonny Island Branching Unit and Cable Landing Station - Nigeria
description: USTDA feasibility study and technical assistance for submarine cable branching unit and cable landing station at Bonny Island, Nigeria. Supports international broadband connectivity infrastructure.

title: TLcom Capital seed investment in uLesson
description: TLcom Capital led a $3.1M seed round in uLesson, a Nigerian edtech startup founded by serial entrepreneur Sim Shagaya (founder of Konga). uLesson delivers affordable, structured K-12 digital learning content across Africa, targeting learners in Nigeria, Kenya, Ghana, Rwanda, Uganda, Sierra Leone, and Liberia via mobile app. This was TLcom's first education sector investment in Africa.

title: Partech Africa Series A equity investment in Nomba (Kudi)
description: Partech Africa led a $5M Series A funding round in Kudi (later renamed Nomba), a Nigerian payment service provider enabling digital payments for small businesses and agents. Kudi provides mobile-based financial services and agency banking across Nigeria. Co-investors include Y Combinator CEO Michael Seibel, Khosla Ventures, and Y Combinator.

title: Visa Equity Investment in Interswitch Nigeria
description: Visa Inc. acquired a significant minority equity stake (~20%) in Interswitch Group, Nigeria's leading digital payments company, for approximately $200 million. The investment valued Interswitch at $1 billion, making it Nigeria's first fintech unicorn. As part of the strategic partnership, Visa and Interswitch committed to advancing the digital payments ecosystem across Africa.

title: 9mobile (EMTS) Turnaround Debt Facility
description: AFC approved a USD 230 million senior debt facility (super senior debt investment) to 9mobile (Emerging Markets Telecommunications Services / EMTS, formerly Etisalat Nigeria), Nigeria's fourth-largest mobile network operator. The facility is structured in two tranches: (i) to repay historic vendor obligations, finance costs, and interest reserve account; and (ii) quick-win capex initiatives for network infrastructure upgrade. Purpose is to support 9mobile's turnaround strategy and reposition it for growth and profitability in Nigeria's competitive telecoms market.

title: Establishment of a National Rural Broadband Network (NRBN)
description: Government of India Line of Credit to Nigeria for establishment of a National Rural Broadband Network (NRBN). The LoC was approved by India's Department of Economic Affairs (DEA) on 18 June 2019 and MEA go-ahead granted 25 June 2019. The project aims to extend broadband connectivity to rural and underserved communities across Nigeria through deployment of ICT infrastructure. NRBN implementation is managed by the Federal Ministry of Communications.

title: Partech Africa Series A equity investment in TradeDepot
description: Partech Africa's recently launched Africa Fund led a $3M Series A round in TradeDepot, a Nigeria-based SaaS platform connecting FMCG consumer goods brands to informal retailers across Africa. This was Partech Africa's first portfolio investment. The round supports expansion of TradeDepot's footprint in Nigeria and development in other African markets.

title: North West InfraCo and Data Center Feasibility Study - Nigeria
description: USTDA feasibility study for data center development in North West Nigeria (InfraCo). Covers data center design, ICT infrastructure and telecommunications integration.

title: MTN Nigeria Capital Expenditure Equipment Facility
description: AFC served as mandated lead arranger and contributed funding of up to USD 80 million as part of a USD 100 million three-year term loan facility arranged in conjunction with Rand Merchant Bank (RMB). The funding was designated to support MTN Nigeria Communications' capital expenditure, primarily for essential network equipment in Nigeria. MTN Nigeria is the country's largest mobile network operator. The facility supports expansion of voice and data network coverage across Nigeria.

title: 4DX Ventures Series A equity investment in Tizeti
description: 4DX Ventures led a $3M Series A funding round in Tizeti (Wifi.com.ng), a Nigerian Internet Service Provider offering unlimited broadband wifi internet access in Nigeria and Ghana. Tizeti's 4G LTE network uses solar-powered base stations to provide affordable internet to homes and businesses. The funding supports network expansion in Nigeria and growth into Ghana. Co-investors include Y Combinator Continuity, Social Capital, Lynnet Capital, and Golden Palm Investments.

title: China Eximbank and Credit Suisse AG provide $84 million syndicated buyer's credit facility for MTN Nigeria Communications to facilitate acquisition of telecommunication equipment from Huawei
description: In April 2017, China Eximbank and Credit Suisse AG signed an $84 million syndicated buyer's credit facility agreement with MTN Nigeria Communications Ltd. to facilitate its acquisition of telecommunication equipment from Huawei. This loan carries an interest rate of LIBOR plus a margin of 5.5%. The proceeds from the loan were used to finance 85% of the the value of a $106 million contract with Huawei. It is repayable in 8 equal installments beginning August 2018. The loan achieved a 100% disbursement rate.

title: CPCIF Strategic Minority Stake in Venture Garden Nigeria — Fintech Platform
description: Convergence Partners Communications Infrastructure Fund (CPCIF) invested $20 million for a strategic minority stake in Venture Garden Nigeria (VGN), a diversified fintech holding company with significant operations in Nigeria. VGN provides innovative, data-driven, end-to-end technology platforms addressing reconciliation and payment processing inefficiencies across multiple industry verticals including financial services, education, aviation, power, downstream oil and gas, and cybersecurity. Investment was made at CPCIF final close (capital over $200 million). Venture Garden Group later incubated companies including Flutterwave, Helium Health, AppZone, and GreenHouse Capital.

recipient: INT Towers Limited (IHS Towers Nigeria subsidiary)
title: INT Towers Nigeria — Equity Investment (Telecoms Tower Infrastructure)
description: BII invested $20M equity in INT Towers Limited in February 2015. INT Towers owns and operates over 9,100 telecoms towers across seven regions in Nigeria and is a wholly owned subsidiary of the IHS Towers Group. The investment enables mobile network operators to provide 2G/3G/4G connectivity to Nigerian consumers and businesses. Investment exited by September 2019.

title: IHS Nigeria Tower Expansion Loan (2015)
description: IFC provided a $50 million loan to IHS Nigeria Plc to finance the acquisition and upgrade of 2,705 towers from Etisalat Nigeria (now 9mobile) in a Buy and Lease Back (BLB) arrangement. IHS Nigeria is the largest tower company in Nigeria operating over 30,000 towers across the country. The investment enabled IHS to expand its portfolio significantly and provide 2G/3G/4G infrastructure to mobile network operators, supporting connectivity for millions of Nigerians.
